notes: Walking an ArrayList is in the course. Topic 4.9 is five concepts and fifteen exercises about the indexed loop, the enhanced for, and the two ways removing while you walk goes wrong. Those two are separated on purpose, because they are the same mistake in different loops and they fail completely differently: the indexed one skips an element and hands back a wrong answer without complaining, and the enhanced for stops the program. Knowing not to remove while looping is no use if you cannot tell which of those you are looking at.

Changing a list inside an enhanced for now stops, the way Java stops. The interpreter did not have this at all, so a lesson could animate a loop quietly skipping elements when the real program throws ConcurrentModificationException on the second turn. It is Java's actual iterator now, which means it also gets the two cases that do not throw right: replacing an element is legal, and a removal that happens to leave nothing left to fetch finishes quietly, which is where the belief that any of this is safe comes from.
The trap lessons animate the exception rather than describing it. Both removal traps and the off by one now run to the point where the program stops and show it stopping.
